We cut customer onboarding from 14 days to 3.

The fix wasn't software. It was one shared Google Doc.

Before, every new client got 6 emails from 4 different people on our team. Nobody knew what had been sent. Clients asked the same questions three times.

So we killed the emails. Every client now gets one living doc on day one: who to call, what happens this week, what we need from them.

Two things surprised me:

1. Support tickets in month one dropped by half. Most questions were already answered in the doc.
2. Clients started editing it themselves. One added a section for their own IT team.

The lesson I keep relearning: most process problems are really "where does the truth live?" problems.

What's one thing in your onboarding that clients keep asking about?
